Repair of other personal and household goods (ISIC 9529) — Operator Console

read-only sample · every row generated at build time by running the real actor · repair completion and item return are always human-approved

What this page is

Generated by clojure -M:dev:render-html, which executes 22 real requests through specialtyrepair.operation's langgraph StateGraph (langgraph.graph/run*) against this repo's own seed data (specialtyrepair.store/demo-data) and renders what it observed. Watches, jewelry and bicycles — the goods this ISIC class covers — put two independent hazards in one shop: an unsafe repair that goes back to a customer, and a precious-metal repair whose hallmark integrity was never confirmed. Both are HARD holds below.

The build refuses to write this file unless every hold rule declared in the actor's own source was actually raised by the real governor, and every human approval the scenario issued was actually observed with a named approver. Nothing on this page is a placeholder; where a value could not be measured, the cell says so instead of guessing.

Governor rule coverage — every declared rule, actually raised

The rule set is DERIVED at build time by reading this actor's own source (specialtyrepair/governor.cljc, specialtyrepair/operation.cljc) for :rule literals, so a rule added tomorrow enters this table by itself. The build throws if any declared rule stayed silent — a bare “at least one hold” check would let this page stay green while the governor grew rules nobody exercised. All of these are HARD: a human approver cannot override them, and the proposal never reaches the approval node.

Human approvals — and where the approver actually survived

Joined from the :approval-granted facts the run emitted on its :audit channel (which lives under :state, not at the top level of the g/run* result). The last two columns are measured, not asserted: for each approved op the build reads the register the commit actually landed in and looks for a key whose name carries an approver. “audit only” means the approval genuinely happened and a named human granted it, but the durable record does not carry the name — which is a different statement from “nobody approved”, and this page will not conflate the two. If a register cannot be read at all, the cell says so rather than reporting an absence.

Jurisdiction spec-basis catalog

The G2-style citation table specialtyrepair.governor checks every :jurisdiction/assess proposal against. A jurisdiction not in this table has NO spec-basis, full stop — the advisor must not fabricate one, and the run above shows what happens when it tries. The hallmark column is deliberately empty for Japan: this R0 catalog records no mandatory statutory hallmarking/assay-office regime there, and inventing one to make coverage look bigger is the exact fabrication this discipline forbids.
